size.note: Wikipedia gives 32–37 cm, with a wingspan of 78–90 cm.

summary: A long-distance migrant that winters in East Africa, including eastern South Africa, and Madagascar. Adults are blue-grey and lack the black underwing coverts of Eleonora’s Falcon. The shape is a large Eurasian Hobby or a small Eleonora’s Falcon, with long pointed wings, a long tail and a slim body. The young bird has a dark trailing edge to the wings and tail. Wikipedia does not describe the voice in the text used here. Status and months were left unset. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: A young Sooty Falcon is described as like a large juvenile Eurasian Hobby, distinguished by the dark trailing edge of the wings and tail.

sources.title: The Atlas of Southern African Birds, Vol. 1 (Sooty Falcon)

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^2=4 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 2–8.

Long pointed wings. The adult lacks black underwing coverts.
Blue-grey below. The young bird shows a dark trailing edge.

calls.description: The Wikipedia text used here does not describe the voice. Grade A call from Duba, Saudi Arabia. The filename names Sooty Falcon.

research.note: No Newman page was found. Wikipedia says it winters in eastern South Africa. Population figures were left unchanged. Status is palearctic-migrant: SABAP1 says it migrates from breeding grounds in the eastern Sahara and Arabian Peninsula to Madagascar and southern Africa.
